title: May Admin Architecture Alignment — Framework v2 Compliance Review
authority: PROJECT_CONSTITUTION.md; S208 Board A Frozen Principles; May Admin (S252-S262)

knowledge/REVISION_HISTORY.md S254-S257 — reliability hardening and MVP readiness
summary: May Admin (S252-S262) is well-aligned with Framework v2 architectural principles. All modules consume from authoritative registries, maintain traceability chains, and integrate with governance guard. Operational gaps (student data, challenge triage) are deployment issues, not architectural misalignment.

framework_v2_alignment.p2_scan_once: Cross-engine audit confirms all engines consume from consistent registry sources

p1_identity_before_trust.evidence: All modules use QID-based identity resolution through registry lookups. No module trusts QID alone without cross-referencing registry context.

p2_scan_once_consume_many.evidence: All modules consume from registries, not raw pack files. Investigation API, Question Lookup, and Session Intelligence use generated artifacts. The only exception is the delivery mechanism (app.js) which reads raw packs for rendering — this is the design intent (runtime authority).
p2_scan_once_consume_many.note: Delivery mechanism (app.js) reads raw pack files for rendering — this is by design (CAQS §1.4: runtime AI never determines correctness; scoring authority lives with the application). The read is from raw files but is read-only and functionally necessary.

p3_delta_review.evidence: May Admin tools are not in the certification pipeline. Delta review applies to content certification waves, not administrative tooling.

p4_readiness_before_certification.evidence: S257 MVP Readiness Board evaluated all 5 modules against 6 automatic stop conditions before recommending Phase 1 implementation. All 6 stop conditions PASS. Readiness gating applied to admin tools.

p5_governance_automation.evidence: May Admin tools integrate with governance guard. Investigation creation, recommendation generation, and challenge resolution write through governance guard paths. All 6 rules apply to admin-initiated writes.

p6_traceability_everywhere.evidence: All 5 core modules maintain traceability through registries. Investigation chains (challenge→defect→recommendation→session→certification) verified across 8/8 cases with 0 manual report traversal. 1 anomaly (P1-EC-004) detected and tracked — traceability is working.
p6_traceability_everywhere.anomaly: P1-EC-004 state inconsistency — detection proves traceability, resolution pending

s257_readiness_board.conditions: 4 conditions (C1-C4 per S257), all non-blocking for Phase 1 start

operational_gaps.impact: 23 challenges unattended — reduces investigative value but doesn't block platform operation
Student Exposure Index and adaptive learning features cannot operate
operational_gaps.remediation: Requires production deployment. Not a May Admin architectural issue.

operational_gaps.impact: Analytics completeness reduced but traceability intact

may_admin_readiness.note: All identified gaps are operational, not architectural. May Admin is well-aligned with Framework v2 principles.

integration_with_framework_v2.certification_pipeline: May Admin does not feed into content certification — it consumes certification decisions retroactively. Investigation findings feed into the governance process via defect library updates, not directly into certification.
integration_with_framework_v2.governance_guard: May Admin write paths (investigation creation, recommendation generation) pass through governance guard. Admin tools are not exempt from structural rules.
integration_with_framework_v2.registry_consumption: All modules are registered as consumers in SESSION208_REGISTRY_AUTHORITY.json. No unregistered consumption paths.
integration_with_framework_v2.future_integration: S208 Board C expansion rule MA-R1 requires all new admin features to consume from authoritative registries. MA-R4 requires governance guard integration on all write paths.
